pool.text: A data set has \( Q_1 = 20 \), \( Q_3 = 50 \). Which value is an outlier by the IQR rule?

pool.text: A school wants to test whether a new tutoring programme improves exam scores. (a) Design a completely randomised experiment using 60 volunteer students. (b) Identify one potential confounding variable and explain how randomisation addresses it. (c) Explain why volunteers may limit the scope of inference.
pool.sol: (a) Number students 1–60. Use a random number generator to assign 30 to treatment (tutoring) and 30 to control (no tutoring). Compare mean exam scores after the programme. (b) Prior knowledge level is a confounder; randomisation distributes it roughly equally between groups on average. (c) Volunteers may be more motivated than typical students, so results may not generalise to all students (scope limited to similar motivated populations).
